summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored documents: São Tomé and Príncipe (Decree-Law 7/2025 and four programme web pages), Bulgaria (Citizenship Act and Foreigners Act as consolidated in 2026, the 2022 repeal bill, a US Treasury sanctions release), Comoros (four IMF documents), Cambodia (1996 and 2018 nationality laws, the 2025 amendment and Sub-decree 225, all but the first scanned Khmer read by OCR) and the Netherlands (2019 parliamentary answers, the 2021 abolition letter, Staatsblad 2024/83). Mostly rules: fees, deadlines, holding periods and eligibility ages. New numbers: Comoros ECP windfall, savings and allocations in 2012, three IMF HIPC revenue rows, São Tomé's nationality count and advertised processing times, and Malta passport counts by region relayed in the Dutch answers.

program_terms.quote: យ៉ាងហោចរយៈពេល ៦ ( ប្រាំមួយ )ខែ
program_terms.notes: Scanned Khmer text; quote from OCR (tesseract khm, 300 dpi), spacing may differ. Translation: 'at least 6 (six) full months'. Donation in cash to the national budget for socio-economic development or the humanitarian sector; amount set by sub-decree.

program_terms.applies_to: General Department of Identification: examination of a naturalisation file (all naturalisation routes, incl. investment and donation)
program_terms.quote: យ៉ាងយូរ៤៥(សែសិបប្រាំ )ថ្ងៃនៃថ្ងៃធ្វើការ
program_terms.notes: Scanned Khmer text; quote from OCR (tesseract khm, 300 dpi). Translation: 'within at most 45 (forty-five) working days'. If incomplete, the applicant is told in writing to correct within 30 working days, and the Department continues within 15 working days of receiving the corrections. Grant is by Royal Decree on the Prime Minister's proposal (Art. 27); ID and passport only after the oath (Art. 28). Application fee to be set by an inter-ministerial prakas (Art. 26; no amount here).

program_terms.applies_to: applicant for naturalisation: time to correct an incomplete file after written notice
program_terms.quote: កែតម្រូវក្នុងរយៈពេលយ៉ាងយូរ៣០( សាមសិប )ថ្ងៃនៃថ្ងៃធ្វើការ
program_terms.notes: Scanned Khmer text; quote from OCR. Translation: 'to correct within at most 30 (thirty) working days'.

program_terms.applies_to: minor children in a family naturalisation application: criminal record certificate required from age 14 to under 18
program_terms.quote: ប្រសិនបើកូននោះមានអាយុចាប់ពី១៤(ដប់បួន)ឆ្នាំ ដល់ក្រោម១៨(ដប់ប្រាំបី )ឆ្នាំ
program_terms.notes: Scanned Khmer text; quote from OCR. Translation: 'if the child is aged from 14 (fourteen) to under 18 (eighteen)'.

program_terms.applies_to: naturalisation in Malta, as described by Dutch MPs in a parliamentary question
program_terms.quote: waarbij iemand zich voor 900.000 euro kan laten naturaliseren tot Maltees
program_terms.notes: Members' description in a written question (2 Oct 2019), not an official Maltese figure; the government's answer does not repeat it.

program_terms.applies_to: investor: one of the added-value criteria (two of three must be met): at least 10 jobs created within five years
program_terms.quote: Binnen vijf jaar worden ten minste 10 arbeidsplaatsen gecreëerd
program_terms.notes: RVO tests added value: two of (a) at least 10 jobs within 5 years, (b) more innovation in the Dutch company, (c) other non-financial added value (knowledge, networks, customers, active involvement). Policy as described on 28 Nov 2019; start date not given here. FIU checks in the Netherlands and the country of origin are mandatory.

events.title: Government sends Parliament a bill to end citizenship for investors
events.description: According to the 2022 motives, the Council of Ministers approved and on 8 Oct 2019 submitted to the National Assembly changes removing naturalisation for people with permanent residence under art. 25(1) items 6 and 7 of the Foreigners Act (and their family members, or who raised the investment to at least BGN 2 million). Parliament instead kept investor citizenship and residence with more controls (DV 21 of 2021).
events.quote: Министерският съвет одобри и внесе на  8 октомври 2019 г. в Народното събрание предложения за промени в режима за придобиване на българско гражданство срещу инвестиции

events.title: Parliament keeps investor citizenship but tightens control (DV 21 of 2021)
events.description: The amending law adopted by the 44th National Assembly (State Gazette no. 21 of 2021) kept citizenship and permanent residence for investors while increasing control over investors, instead of abolishing them as the government had proposed in 2019. Date is the State Gazette issue date used elsewhere in the dataset for DV 21/2021.
events.quote: се запази възможността за придобиване на българско гражданство и за даване на разрешение за постоянно пребиваване срещу инвестиции, като се увеличи възможността за контрол върху инвеститорите

events.title: European Commission writes again about Bulgarian investor citizenship
events.description: A further letter from the European Commission in June 2021 expressed concern that Bulgarian law still allowed naturalisation in exchange for predetermined payments, citing Article 20 TFEU; the government cites it as a reason for repealing arts. 12a and 14a.
events.quote: получено поредно писмо от юни 2021 г. от Европейската комисия

events.title: IMF: ECP revenue fell steeply in 2013 after tighter controls
events.description: The IMF says the programme sells passports to foreign nationals in some Middle Eastern countries, mainly the United Arab Emirates, under bilateral agreements, and that revenue declined steeply in 2013 after tighter controls were imposed in response to earlier irregularities. In 2013 the government spent ECP proceeds accumulated at the central bank in 2012 on capital spending.
events.location: Staff report para 4 and footnote 1; Annex footnote 3
events.quote: Revenues from the program declined steeply in 2013 following the imposition of tighter controls in response to earlier irregularities.

events.title: Authorities hope for a new ECP agreement with Kuwait
events.description: During the 2014 Article IV discussions the authorities said they were optimistic that a new ECP programme with Kuwait would be agreed; IMF staff urged that such volatile revenue be budgeted prudently, ring-fenced and protected by strong safeguards against misuse.
events.quote: The authorities indicated that they were optimistic that a new ECP program with Kuwait would be agreed.

events.title: Amended Nationality Law allows deprivation of citizenship obtained by fraud
events.description: New Art. 29 lets Khmer nationality be withdrawn (by Royal Decree) for treason, harming sovereignty or security, serving a foreign army or state, acquiring nationality by fraud or false information, or conviction for certain crimes; withdrawal from citizens by birth needs age 18+ and another nationality (or the prospect of one) and a national commission's opinion. New Arts. 16 and 27: ID cards and passports are issued only after the oath before the Supreme Court; the oath text is annexed. This confirms the press reports noted on the existing event for this law.
events.location: PDF pp. 3-4 (printed 3/4-4/4), Article One, new Arts. 16, 27 and 29
events.quote: ៤- បានទទួលសញ្ជាតិខ្មែរដោយការក្លែងបន្លំ ឬការផ្តល់ព័ត៌មានមិនពិត។

events.title: Dutch cabinet gives the investor scheme one year to show potential
events.description: Answering MPs' questions on Malta's passport sales, the cabinet says fewer than 10 investor permits have been issued, no abuse is known, and it will see whether adapting the scheme can make it useful for innovative companies; if after one year it shows no such potential it will be abolished (as decided in Jan 2021).
events.quote: Mocht na één jaar blijken dat de regeling deze potentie niet heeft, dan wordt zij afgeschaft.

new_indicators.name: CBI receipts saved, share of GDP
new_indicators.definition: Part of citizenship- or residence-by-investment receipts in a period that the government saves (keeps on deposit or uses to reduce net credit) rather than spends, divided by GDP, as stated by the source.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-misc2 for the IMF 2012 Article IV on Comoros (ECP windfall: 1.8% of GDP saved in 2012). No existing indicator covers savings out of CBI receipts as a flow.

ledger.contains: News item on the programme website (cip.gov.st), 2 Mar 2026, headed 'First 200 Applications': more than 220 applications from over 27 nationalities since launch, with promotional text on due diligence and the National Transformation Fund; no approvals, revenue or breakdown. Page footer lists teasers for other news items (China roadshow, IMI Connect Barcelona, blockchain-enabled programme Sept 2025, three generators bought through the NTF, UNESCO biosphere label, GlobeVisa conference Oct 2025, launch conference, Dubai office Sept 2025), which are separate articles not stored here. The 220 applications row was already in the data; the nationalities count added.

News item on the programme website, 2 Jan 2026: national conference in October 2025 formally introducing the programme, attended by the Prime Minister, the Minister of Justice and the CIU director; contributions said to go to renewable energy, infrastructure, education and eco-tourism, with generators bought from programme money shown. No amounts or counts. Already in the data as a launch event; footer teasers for other news items are not part of this article.

Programme website page 'Donation to the National Transformation Fund' (read 2 Oct 2026): contribution paid after approval in principle; fund priorities (renewable energy, eco-tourism, education and infrastructure, deep sea port; no amounts); fee box (USD 5,000 submission fee per application, USD 90,000 single, USD 95,000 family of 2-4, USD 5,000 per extra dependant, USD 750 per applicant for documents); six-step process; FAQ (age 18+, dependants: children up to 30, parents/grandparents from 55; no residence requirement; sponsor due diligence USD 5,000; approval in about 2 months and passport 3-4 months after approval). USD 90,000 and USD 750 were already in the data; the other fees, the eligibility ages and the advertised processing times are added.

Programme website page 'Post-Approval Inclusion Fees' (read 2 Oct 2026): fees only for dependants added after approval in principle (submission fee $5,000 except newborns, spouse $10,000, each other dependant $5,000, newborn up to 1 year $500), application steps, and the same FAQ as the NTF page (extracted once, from stp-cip-web-ntf-2026). Amounts are printed with a bare '$', so recorded with currency unspecified; the Decree-Law gives the same amounts in USD (stated in notes).

Decree-Law No. 07/2025 (Diário da República I Série No. 33, 1 Aug 2025, 12 PDF pages; approved 10 May 2025, promulgated 28 Jul 2025, in force on publication): regulation of nationality by investment or donation (RNID). Creates the UCID (under the Justice Minister), the programme (PCID), agent licensing (unlicensed promotion fined up to USD 500,000), the National Transformation Fund and its bank account rules (BBB- rating abroad, 10% guarantee, monthly reporting, annual published audit), a Review Committee chaired by the Public Prosecutor; applicant requirements (18+, medical certificate, criminal record under 3 months, records for 5 years), deadlines (15-day preliminary review, 15-day decision after the Prosecutor's prior approval, 90 days to pay the FNT contribution, 5 days to registry, 6 months for Prosecutor's opposition), voluntary extra investment in public projects (Annex II list of 13 project areas, no amounts), military service exemption, possible exclusion of nationalities, sanctions (fine up to 20% of the investment), annual and quarterly reporting duties, ministers may change Annex I amounts. Annex I: agent licence USD 5,000 a year, due diligence and processing USD 5,000 per application, contributions USD 90,000 / 95,000 / 5,000 per extra dependant, post-approval additions USD 10,000 spouse, 5,000 other dependants, 500 newborn. Annex III: documents list. No statistics. Five Annex I amounts and two events were already in the data; all other amounts and time limits now added.

Bulgarian Citizenship Act, consolidated text on lex.bg (as of DV 55/2026): acquisition by descent, birth and naturalisation (art. 12: 5 years' permanent or long-term residence, language, income, no convictions; art. 13 3-year routes; art. 15 Bulgarian origin; art. 16 special merit or state interest, no amount), loss, revocation, procedure, registers. Arts. 12a and 14a (investor routes) are shown only as repealed (DV 26/2022) with no text, so no investment amounts; transitional provisions of DV 26/2022: pending procedures terminated (§ 7), investor citizens must report investment changes within 14 days and keep investments 2 years (art. 14a) or 1 year (art. 12a) after naturalisation, or naturalisation may be revoked (§ 8, printed twice as § 8 and § 9). Also a 2013 transitional item asking the economy minister to issue the art. 14a(4) ordinance. No statistics. Events (2013 fast-track, 2022 repeal) were already in the data; the holding periods, notification deadline and the ordinary 5-year route now added as terms.

Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act, consolidated text on lex.bg (as of DV 55/2026): entry, visas, all residence categories, EU Blue Card, start-up visa, digital nomads, family members, refusal and withdrawal, fines, procedures. Investor content: long-term residence for BGN 600,000 in real estate (art. 24(1) item 19, loan up to 25%) or BGN 250,000 in disadvantaged regions with 5 jobs (item 20); permanent residence for BGN 2 million listed securities, BGN 1 million concessions, BGN 1 million funds (with BGN 5 million / 3 million fund-size floors), BGN 2 million priority project, BGN 6 million unlisted company, certified investment-promotion activity (item 13, no amount), BGN 500,000 plus 10 jobs (item 16), and after 5 years on items 19/20 (item 17); Investment Agency pre-check (art. 25(7)-(10)); 5-year holding for items 6, 8, 16 and no use as loan collateral (art. 25(11)-(12)); withdrawal if the investment is reduced; decision in 2 months (+2); spouses of investor permanent residents exempt from the residence requirement (art. 25(1) item 2). Art. 25a residence for merit or state interest (no amount). No statistics. Six art. 25(1) item 6-8 amounts were already in the data; the other investor amounts and rules now added. Other numbers (general fines, deadlines for other categories) are out of scope.

Bill file 47-202-01-2 sent to the National Assembly (cover letter dated '18.01.2021', evidently 2022; Council of Ministers Decision No. 12 of 14 Jan 2022; draft law; motives). Draft: repeal arts. 12a and 14a, related amendments, and a transitional rule that pending applications be decided under the old rules (the law as adopted instead terminated them). Motives: Commission report of 23 Jan 2019; residence periods before naturalisation (5 years art. 12a, 1 year art. 14a, 3 years for the investor's spouse) while investors stayed only days or weeks; most applicants held government securities or trust deposits over BGN 1 million, raised to BGN 2 million, often sold before naturalisation; checks hindered by bank and tax secrecy; the 2019 government bill and Parliament's 2021 choice to keep the scheme with more control; Commission letter of June 2021; no budget impact. The annexes listed (impact assessment, consultation reports) are not in this file. No statistics. Bill approval was already an event; residence periods, the BGN 1 million thresholds and three dated events now added.

US Treasury press release JY0208 (2 Jun 2021): Global Magnitsky sanctions on three Bulgarian individuals (Vassil Bojkov, Delyan Peevski, Ilko Zhelyazkov) and 64 entities, with the lists of companies. Programme content is one passage: from early 2018 Peevski and Zhelyazkov ran a scheme selling Bulgarian residency documents, with company representatives paying bribes so clients got citizenship documents immediately instead of making the '$500,000 deposit' or waiting five years. The scheme is already an event; the deposit (currency unspecified, bare '$') and five-year wait are added as described terms. The rest (gambling, elections, entity lists) is out of scope.

IMF Country Report 13/32 (Comoros 2012 Article IV and fourth ECF review, Feb 2013; HTML, about 11,400 lines incl. tables, Fund relations, DSA, letter of intent, MEFP and TMU). Programme content: the footnote repeated under most tables that 2011-12 revenue includes ECP receipts of about 3% of GDP a year; Text Figure 1 note (2012 about 3%); para 8 and MEFP para 3 on 2012 (ECP receipts projected at 4.5% of GDP against a 1.4% programme target, windfall 3.1%, 1.8% saved, 1% to transport infrastructure and malaria/HIV, 0.2% short-term loan to the oil importer); para 12 (4% in 2011-12, return to about 2% in 2013); the ECP feeding the narrowing of the current account deficit (no ECP number); TMU footnote defining the ECP (2008, KMF 1 million, about US$3,000, receipts routed via the Banque de France). The fiscal tables have no separate ECP line (it sits inside nontax revenue), so no KMF amounts. The 3%, 4%, 4.5%, 1.4%, 2% rows and the KMF 1 million term were already in the data; the windfall, savings and allocation figures are added (one new indicator proposed: cbi_revenue_saved_pct_gdp). The rest of the report (growth, inflation, debt, reserves, structural reforms) is out of scope.

IMF Country Report 15/34 (Comoros 2014 Article IV, Feb 2015; HTML with tables, DSA and annexes). Programme content: 2013 fiscal outturn shaped by spending ECP proceeds accrued at the central bank in 2012; non-tax revenue down 3.2 points of GDP in 2013 'mainly' because of the ECP contraction (not an ECP figure, so not recorded); credit growth from drawing down ECP proceeds; reserves peak of KMF 72.7 billion in 2012 'owing to' remittances and ECP (not an ECP figure); new ECP with Kuwait hoped for; Annex III para 4: ECP receipts more than 6% of GDP in 2012 (already in the data); footnotes describing the ECP (passports sold mainly to the UAE under bilateral agreements; steep decline in 2013 after tighter controls). The fiscal tables have no separate ECP line. Two events added; the rest of the report is out of scope.

IMF/IDA Enhanced HIPC Initiative Completion Point Document for Comoros (IMF Country Report 13/33, Feb 2013; HTML with debt relief tables, DSA, triggers). Programme content: para 10 (domestic primary surplus of 2.2% of GDP in 2012 including ECP revenue, a general fiscal figure; ECP windfalls averaging 3% of GDP in 2011-12 thanks to ties with Gulf partners), footnote 5 (ECP: citizenship for KMF 1 million), and the Text Table 1 / Table 1a footnote (2011-12 revenue includes ECP receipts of about 3% of GDP each year). Gulf creditors (Kuwait, UAE debt relief) are not about the programme. No ECP line in the tables. Nothing from this document was in the data; three revenue rows and the KMF 1 million term added.

IMF Country Report 09/307 (Comoros: assessment under the post-conflict emergency assistance and PRGF request, 2009; HTML with tables, letter of intent and MEFP). The only programme content is MEFP para 17: 2009 domestic revenue plan includes exceptional ECP revenue of 0.8% of GDP (already in the data, status budget) plus 0.3% of GDP from new biometric passport sales (ordinary passports, not the programme). Gulf bilateral assistance and Kuwait/UAE creditor lines are not about the programme. Nothing further in scope.

English translation (4 pp., MLMUPC/ADB) of the 1996 Law on Nationality: nationality by birth and marriage (3 years), naturalisation conditions (good conduct, clean record, 7 years' residence, Khmer language and history; 3 years if born in Cambodia), exemption from residence for investors spending 1,250,000,000 riels (with or without CDC approval), donation route of 1,000,000,000 riels to the national budget, special merit, family applications (children under 18), Khmer name, Royal Decree, oath, renunciation, penalties for illegal ID or passports (5-10 years' prison). No statistics. Both amounts and the launch were already in the data; the family age rule added.

Law on Nationality, Royal Kram NS/RKM/0618/008 of 21 Jun 2018 (10 scanned pages in Khmer, read by OCR with the khm model; p. 2 blank): definitions (naturalisation based on residence, investment, cash donation or special merit), Ministry of Interior competence, nationality by birth, adoption and marriage (3 years plus 12 months' residence), naturalisation (Art. 19: conduct, record, 7 years' residence for immigrants, Khmer language; 3 years if born in Cambodia), investor route (Art. 21: 12 months' legal residence, amount and sectors by sub-decree), donation route (Art. 22: 6 months, amount by sub-decree), special merit (Art. 23), family applications, Khmer name, Royal Decree, oath, renunciation (age 18), penalties for false ID and passports (2-10 years' prison, fines KHR 4-10 million for individuals and 10-100 million for legal persons; out of scope), transitional and repeal of the 1996 law. No amounts for the routes and no statistics. The rule change was already an event; the two residence periods added as terms.

Law on the Amendment of the Law on Nationality, Royal Kram NS/RKM/0925/030 of 5 Sep 2025 (5 scanned pages in Khmer, read by OCR with the khm model; p. 2 nearly blank; adopted by the National Assembly 25 Aug 2025). Amends Arts. 1, 7, 16, 27, 28, 29 and 34 of the 2018 law: adds deprivation (withdrawal) of nationality, including for nationality obtained by fraud or false information; ID and passport only after the oath; renunciation at 18+; annex with the oath text. No amounts or statistics; the routes and amounts are untouched. The promulgation was already an event (with a caveat that the content was unverified); an event describing the verified content is added.

Sub-decree No. 225 on the implementation of the Law on Nationality (dated 1 Dec 2025; 19 scanned pages in Khmer, read by OCR with the khm model, annex re-read at 400 dpi). Contents: procedure and documents for claiming nationality by marriage (12 months' residence, 45/30/15 working-day review steps, appeal within 30 working days); naturalisation procedure and documents for residence, investment, donation and special-merit routes, spouses and minor children (criminal record from age 14), 45-working-day review, fee by inter-ministerial prakas (no amount), Royal Decree, oath before ID and passport; investment route: own capital of at least KHR 4,000,000,000 actually spent, in priority sectors and project types listed in the annex, plus tax compliance and an investment plan, assessed by the Ministry of Interior, lawful source of funds (Arts. 29-30); donation route: personal cash donation of at least KHR 12,000,000,000 to the national budget via the Ministry of Economy and Finance (Art. 31); renunciation (30/30/10 working days); deprivation of nationality and a 15-member national commission; repeal of Sub-decree 112 of 2018 (Art. 58); in force from signature. Annex: 12 priority sectors and project types (agriculture, agro-industry, food processing, import-substituting manufacturing, tourism, digital, high-tech/R&D, SMEs and industrial/science parks, high value-added manufacturing, regional and global value chains, SME finance, affordable housing; the last line is cut off in the scan). No statistics. Both amounts and two events were already in the data; review deadlines and the age-14 criminal record rule added.

Aanhangsel Handelingen II 2019/20 nr. 867 (8 pp.): 30 written questions by D66 MPs on Malta's passport sales and answers by the Foreign Minister and others (received 28 Nov 2019). Programme numbers: Malta (relayed from the ORiip report of Nov 2018): 961 'passports' issued to 1 Jul 2018 and a regional split of passport issuance 1 Jul 2015-1 Jul 2018 (Europe 266, Asia 70, Gulf 67, Africa 36, North America 20, Middle East 16, South America 4, Caribbean 3, Oceania 1; no total printed); the MPs' EUR 900,000 price; Netherlands investor scheme: fewer than 10 permits (already in the data), RVO added-value test (10 jobs within 5 years among three criteria), one-year review before abolition. Also the EC's count of member states with citizenship (3) and residence (20) schemes (lists, not programme numbers), Malta's due diligence, the Caruana Galizia inquiry, a Groningen professor (not named here), AIVD warnings. Added: 10 Malta rows (status reported), two terms, one event.

Kamerstuk 30 573 nr. 182 (1 p.): letter of 11 Jan 2021 from the State Secretary for Justice: after the one-year review announced in Nov 2019, the cabinet decides to abolish the scheme for foreign investors because it cannot be adapted while keeping safeguards against abuse; the change to the Aliens Decree is expected in the second half of 2021 (it took effect only in April 2024); the EC expert group report on investor schemes stalled in 2020; the Commission announced infringement procedures against Cyprus and Malta on 20 Oct 2020. No numbers. The abolition decision and the Cyprus/Malta infringement are already events in the data.

Staatsblad 2024 no. 83 (25 pp.): Decree of 9 Apr 2024 (published 16 Apr 2024, in force the next day) amending the Aliens Decree 2000, the Civic Integration Decree 2021 and the Foreign Nationals Employment Decree 2022, with explanatory note. Programme content: deletion of the residence ground for wealthy foreigners (art. 3.29a Vb 2000; Articles I B, D, G, II, III), transitional law keeping existing permits valid and renewable (Article IV), and the note's history (scheme from 1 Oct 2013, at least EUR 1,250,000 invested in an innovative company per Vc B11/2.2, fewer than ten permits granted). The rest (family reunification fraud checks, researcher mobility, mvv exemptions, EU directive fixes, detention hearings, consultation responses) is out of scope. The amount, the permit count and the launch were already in the data (the closure on 17 Apr 2024 is an event from another source); nothing new to add.
